title: READ: Robust and Efficient Anomaly Detection under Data Contamination and Limited Supervision

problem.claim: Anomaly detection methods often require large amounts of training data and incur substantial training-time overhead.

gap.claim: Existing approaches do not adequately exploit the redundancy in unlabeled data to improve training efficiency while maintaining detection performance.

contributions.claim: An end-to-end reinforcement learning framework uses balanced sampling of normal and abnormal instances.
The framework exploits potential anomalies and samples peripheral normal instances to improve anomaly detection without excessive sampling time.
A joint reward mechanism with inconsistency penalties optimizes the agent's action space and representation space for sampling.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report effectiveness and efficiency in extensive experiments on four public datasets from different domains.
The authors report that implementation code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large-data anomaly detection methods can have substantial training-time overhead.
Selecting a small representative subset of unlabeled data may improve efficiency while preserving detection performance.
The framework applies reinforcement learning with balanced sampling, anomaly exploitation, peripheral-normal sampling, and joint reward optimization.
Experiments on four public datasets are reported as demonstrating effectiveness and efficiency.
Code availability is reported through a GitHub repository.

source_observation.claim: A representative subset of unlabeled data may reduce training cost while preserving detection performance.

interpretation.claim: Data selection can be treated as an efficiency mechanism when redundancy is substantial.

application.claim: For large unlabeled anomaly-detection datasets, evaluate representative subset selection alongside full-data training.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when subset selection fails or how much data can be removed safely.

source_observation.claim: The sampling strategy targets both potential anomalies and difficult-to-detect peripheral normal instances.

interpretation.claim: Sampling should account for both rare abnormal examples and ambiguous normal examples.

application.claim: Design sampling policies that explicitly balance anomaly coverage with coverage of hard normal cases.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how anomalies or peripheral normal instances are identified.

unknowns: The abstract does not report dataset names, sizes, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the reinforcement learning algorithm, training procedure, or computational costs.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility beyond the reported code availability.
